text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on April 10, prepared for Reuters by Estonian news agency ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The fire which killed eight elderly women died in a fire in an old people's home in the coastal town of Parnu was probably caused by careless smoking or a power system failure.
- The government will raise electricity rates by one third from May 1, from 45 to 60 cents per kWH. Experts predict no general rise in the cost of living.
- Estonian ballet dancer Stanislaw Yermakov won the grand prix at an international contest in South Africa.
- Teachers of 17 Tallinn schools threaten to on strike on May 10. A 14 percent pay rise has not been paid back-dated from January 1 as promised.

- Retired general Aleksander Einseln accused the security police of taking part in political intrigues and rejected charges of involvment in illegal arms purchases. The daily published an interview with the general.
- Colonel Arvo Sirel is to head the general staff training department, returning to active service after retiring after allegations he was connected to an arms trade scandal in November 1995.
- The state inspection declared that all the transactions of the Bank of Estonia in the years 1993-1995 were legal.
- Estonia and Slovenia may drop visa requirements in May, a foreign ministry spokesman announced.
- The government exhausted all legal ways to help the workers of bankrupt Oru peat plant.
- The defence and environment ministries are still negotiating over the military use of former Soviet Army training grounds, which are located in protected areas.
- The Tallinn municipality may privatise the municipal firm which controls the removal of two thirds of Tallinn waste.
- Heating prices will remain the same in Tallinn until July.
